Subject: MSA/Order Form — derivative rights, telemetry & training language (legal review)

Team / Anya,

Attaching the latest redline from Liminal (redline_MSA_Liminal_v2.docx) and a cleaned Order Form. They’ve pushed back on our standard training consent and want very limited downstream productization language. Key asks from them:

- No explicit ownership of derived products; they want guarantees that any model improvements won’t be used to create competing product modules.
- Strict limits on telemetry/telemetry retention tied to PII minimization and location (EU complaint).
- Opt-out path for training: they want an unconditional opt-out at no extra fee.

From a Redwood perspective the ask list is:
- Preserve our ability to improve models with aggregated feedback/telemetry (non-personal)
- Keep feedback license broad enough for model improvement but narrow for commercial re-use (we usually ask for a non-exclusive, irrevocable license to use feedback to improve services)
- If we allow an opt-out, we need a commercial path (paid opt-out or limited feature-set) and clear operational notes for honoring requests.

Can legal confirm workable clause language for: (1) derived-product carveouts (narrowly tailored), (2) telemetry retention & pseudonymization commitments we can make, and (3) a feedback license that allows model improvement but restricts resale/productization?

Suggested next steps: legal to propose redlines by EOD tomorrow so Sean can signal to the prospect before procurement review. Grace, please add procurement timeline in HubSpot.

Thanks,

Olga Petrov
Senior Deals Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form — derivative rights, telemetry & training language (legal review)

Olga / team / Anya,

Thanks for the context. Quick thoughts after an initial pass on the redline:

1) Derivative / productization. We should offer a two-prong approach: a) a clear definition of "Derived Materials" that excludes (i) output generated for the customer's internal use and (ii) customer-provided training data, and b) a use limitation that allows Redwood to use aggregated and de-identified outputs to improve models but prohibits creating a standalone product that competes with a customer's specific, identified product line for the term of the agreement plus 12 months.

Suggested text snippet (draft): "Redwood may use Customer Feedback and aggregated, de-identified Output to enhance the Service; provided, however, Redwood will not purposefully develop or commercialize a product that is functionally equivalent to Customer's identified product offering during the Term and for 12 months thereafter."

2) Telemetry. Need to align on retention windows and pseudonymization. If Liminal requires EU-only processing, we can agree to limit telemetry routing to EU regions for their account and commit to 30-day retention for raw telemetry, with 12 months for aggregated metrics. Security should confirm feasibility.

3) Training opt-out. We can accept an opt-out but propose a standard commercial trade: either (i) a paid opt-out fee that compensates for lost training signal, or (ii) an opt-out that excludes their traffic from model training but retains access to a slightly older model family (operational complexity flagged).

I’ll produce tracked redlines for the MSA and a clean clause for the Order Form. Looping in Security to confirm telemetry retention and region routing.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form — derivative rights, telemetry & training language (legal review)

Anya — thanks for raising the concerns. Quick note from the commercial side as we balance closing timeline and product constraints.

- We are OK to narrow the derivatives language to avoid giving Redwood a blank check to productize customer-specific workflows. The compromise Laura suggests (12-month ring-fence after term) reads fair to me.
- On training opt-out: I can offer a no-cost opt-out for the pilot (first 6 months) but beyond that we need to charge a nominal fee to cover model improvement economics. Alternatively, we can offer them the opt-out plus an SLA adjustment (slightly longer latency SLO) to incentivize the paid opt-out.
- For telemetry — we can commit to EU-only telemetry routing and the 30-day raw retention, but Security has to confirm whether 30 days is operationally feasible.

Proposed next step: If Laura can push redlines today, I’ll loop Anya and procurement with a clear summary and the proposed opt-out commercial. Would like to avoid a long procurement cycle.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form — derivative rights, telemetry & training language (legal review)

Sean / Olga / Laura,

Appreciate the quick replies and the proposed compromises. A few clarifications from our legal/procurement side after reviewing Laura’s suggestions:

- The 12-month non-compete for functionally equivalent products is a good start but we need more specificity: what constitutes "identified product offering"? Procurement will push back if this is too subjective. We would prefer a carveout that limits Redwood from using model improvements to build features that mimic a "named module" we list in the Order Form.
- On training opt-out: we cannot accept a commercial charge for opt-out in our controls-heavy environment — the vendor must provide an opt-out as a standard privacy control. We're open to a limited performance/SLA trade instead.
- Telemetry routing/retention: EU-only routing and 30-day raw retention are fine, but we need certifiable attestations for retention and deletion (logs/audit). Will require Security ATO evidence.

We’re targeting a procurement decision by 10/20. Can Redwood provide: (1) a redline with Laura’s proposed language, (2) an explicit definition of "named module" approach for the ring-fence, and (3) confirmation from Security on the retention attestations?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if easier.

Best,
Anya Sokolov
Head of Procurement, Liminal Systems
